summary: Three new criminal cases were filed in the Fairbanks court and read for the first time on Tuesday evening, two of them carrying a felony count. Trenton Allen Rix is charged with first-degree burglary, a Class B felony, on an offense recorded in Fairbanks on Nov. 2, and Westley Allen Ingraham is charged with failing to stop for a peace officer while driving recklessly, a Class C felony, with three counts of reckless endangerment, on offenses recorded at North Pole the same day. The court file behind the Nov. 1 arrest of Justin West of Tok is now available and charges him with two counts of second-degree assault, both offenses recorded in October, and one count of fourth-degree assault recorded on Nov. 1. Fairbanks Police added three rows to their bulletins for Oct. 31 and Nov. 1, including an assault and a harassment report with no arrest. The court's weekly criminal filings report, which covers Oct. 27 to Nov. 2, lists 38 cases filed at Fairbanks, four at Nenana, two at Delta Junction and none at Healy; those are the report's own counts and the court has filed at least one case the report omits, 4FA-26-02222CR, which was filed at Fairbanks on Nov. 2 before the report was run. The Alaska Court System's public case database, which was unavailable through Tuesday morning, was responding again by about 5 p.m.

entries.title: Burglary charge: Trenton Allen Rix
body: Trenton Allen Rix is charged with burglary in the first degree - entering a building unlawfully and causing or attempting to cause injury - a Class B felony, punishable by up to 10 years. He is also charged with theft in the fourth degree, taking property worth less than $250, a Class B misdemeanor, and with violating a condition of release on a felony case, a Class A misdemeanor.
The court records all three offenses as having happened in Fairbanks on Nov. 2. The case was filed Nov. 3 and he was arraigned the same afternoon, with a public defender appointed from the bench.
Case 4FA-26-02223CR; preliminary hearing Nov. 12. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Failure to stop for police: Westley Allen Ingraham
body: Westley Allen Ingraham is charged with failure to stop at the direction of a peace officer while driving recklessly - not stopping for an officer and driving recklessly in doing so - a Class C felony, punishable by up to 5 years. He is also charged with reckless driving, which the court records as a misdemeanor not otherwise classified, and with three counts of reckless endangerment, recklessly creating a substantial risk of serious injury, each a Class A misdemeanor.
The court records all five offenses as having happened at North Pole on Nov. 2. The case was filed Nov. 3 and he was arraigned the same afternoon.
Case 4FA-26-02224CR; preliminary hearing Nov. 12. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: False statement charges: Benjaman Charles Cottle
body: Benjaman Charles Cottle is charged with three counts of unsworn falsification in the second degree - a false statement on a form that states the punishment for falsifying it - and one count of giving false information implicating another person in an offense. All four counts are Class A misdemeanors.

The court records the three falsification counts as having happened in Fairbanks on Nov. 15, 2021, and the false information count on Jan. 27, 2022. The case was filed Nov. 2 and a summons was issued to the Alaska State Troopers on Nov. 3; the file records no arrest.
Case 4FA-26-02222CR; no court date has been set. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Justin West
body: Justin West, 35, of Tok was arrested on Nov. 1 and has been charged with two counts of assault in the second degree - intentionally causing physical injury with a dangerous instrument - each a Class B felony, punishable by up to 10 years, and one count of assault in the fourth degree, recklessly causing physical injury, a Class A misdemeanor. The court records all three counts as domestic violence related.

Troopers say they responded to a request for a welfare check at a residence in Tok on Nov. 1 at about 8:40 p.m. and that the investigation resulted in his arrest, and that he was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held pending arraignment.

The court records the offense date of the fourth-degree count as Nov. 1 and the offense dates of the two second-degree counts as Oct. 19 and Oct. 20. Case 4TO-26-00078CR; he was arraigned Nov. 2 at the Fairbanks courthouse and a preliminary hearing is set for Nov. 12. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: DUI arrest: Hunter Joseph Ptacek
body: Hunter Joseph Ptacek, 19, was arrested on a charge of driving under the influence with a blood alcohol level of .08 percent or more and on a second count of a minor consuming, possessing or controlling alcohol, first or second offense, both recorded by police as misdemeanors. 1300 block of College Road, Fairbanks, Nov. 1 at 1:57 a.m.; Fairbanks Police. Police case 26003330.

A court file was opened at Fairbanks the same day, case 4FA-26-02208CR. It records one count as a charging document pending or not filed and states no degree of offense, so no charge class comes from the court. Arraignment Nov. 6. He is arrested, not convicted.

entries.title: Alaska's public court case database was unavailable for much of Tuesday
body: CourtView, the Alaska Court System's public online case database at records.courts.alaska.gov, returned the message "The service is unavailable" to every request made on Nov. 3 between about 3:20 a.m. and about 4:50 a.m. Four pages on the site, including the search page, returned the same message. The site was responding normally again by about 5 p.m.

The site is the only public place where an individual Alaska criminal case file can be looked up by case number or by name. Charges, hearing dates and docket entries are published there and nowhere else.
The three cases newly filed at Fairbanks and the hearing results reported in this edition were read after the site returned.
